neutral_facts.value: The accused was involved in an incident where five persons, including three children, died. The prosecution's case was based on circumstantial evidence, including the testimony of witnesses, an extra-judicial confession, and recovered incriminating items. The accused fled the scene and was later arrested. The post-mortem reports indicated the deaths were due to multiple injuries, and the evidence suggested the accused was responsible for the murders. The accused's conduct, including his false name during arrest and absence of a valid explanation for his actions, supported the prosecution's case. The courts below accepted the evidence as reliable and connected the accused to the crime.

post_offence_conduct.value: absconding from the scene would establish his guilt and rule out hypothesis of innocence. It has come out from the evidence that immediately after the incident, the accused left the village and boarded a bus to Delhi. However, he was arrested in the way by PW-16 at 2.20 a.m., on 28.10.2006. There is no proper explanation by the appellant-accused even u/s 313 statement for his sudden departure from the scene and going to Delhi. In the absence of any reason, the conduct of the appellant supports the case of the prosecution. Further, the appellant, when questioned by PW-16 in the bus, suppressed his original name and gave a false name and only on further interrogation, disclosed his original name. These aspects go against his conduct and support the case of the prosecution

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellant was responsible for the gruesome murders of five persons, including three children, based on circumstantial evidence, extra-judicial confession, recovery of incriminating articles, motive, and the accused's conduct at the time of arrest.

quotes.text: The prosecution has fully established various circumstances which speak about the guilt of the appellant including the recoveries, extra judicial confession, conduct of the appellant mentioning false name at the time of his arrest etc.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that there was no direct eye witness to the incident, the prosecution's case rested on circumstantial evidence, and there were contradictions in the FIR and witness statements. They also contended that the High Court was not justified in restricting remission before 20 years of imprisonment.

quotes.text: There is no direct eye witness to speak about the incident and the case of the prosecution entirely rests upon circumstantial evidence.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that life imprisonment, when imposed for heinous crimes, should be subject to restrictions on remission to ensure the punishment is proportionate and serves the purpose of justice.

quotes.text: The Court would take recourse to the expanded option primarily because in the facts of the case the sentence of 14 years' imprisonment would amount to no punishment at all.
